articles.title: Dem House hopeful endorsed by activist who said 'evil Jews run the world'
articles.summary: Adina Flores, who endorsed Eric Jones for Congress, has posted content about Zionists, Freemasons and LGBTQ ideology across her social media pages.
articles.body: Adina Flores, an activist and a self-proclaimed "civil rights" advocate with a colorful social media presence, is endorsing Eric Jones, the Democratic candidate for Congress in California's 4th Congressional District. The endorsement itself, which focuses on Jones’ promises to combat women’s sexual exploitation, is nothing out of the ordinary. But Flores’ Facebook, Instagram and Substack pages are full of eccentric content that frames political issues as a conflict between race, sexual orientation and secretive sources of influence. The endorsement raises questions for Jones, who has met with Flores multiple times according to social media clips, about whether he agrees with Flores’ views. In one video, posted to Facebook, Flores stated she believed part of California, Sonoma County, was run by Jews. "But we’re literally run by the gay Jewish mafia — the Zionists in Sonoma County. The Jews still run the world. That’s where we’re at," Flores said. "All our money gets sent to Israel, but nobody wants to talk about that." JEWISH COMMUNITY IN DENVER ON HIGH ALERT OVER RISE OF DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST MELAT KIROS "Evil Jews run the world through Masonic Lodges," Flores said in an August Instagram post. "Santa Rosa City Schools is always recruiting for little gay communists. Help save public school enrollment decline by sending your child off to liberal prison indoctrination centers," she said in another post earlier this year. When asked about Flores' comments online, Jones' campaign said he condemns prejudice towards the Jewish community. "I firmly condemn any and all hate toward our Jewish and LGBTQ+ communities. It has no place in our district. My wife is Jewish, we are raising our kids in a Jewish household, I'm a fierce advocate for our public schools and educators, and I have zero tolerance for hateful commentary toward my neighbors or my family," a campaign spokesperson said in a comment to Fox News Digital. Beyond her comment about Jews, in much of her content, Flores bashes what she sees as efforts to indoctrinate kids in LGBTQ+ ideology through control over institutions like schools and local government. "I wasn’t doing any of the wokeness. I stood up for conservative parents. So right now, look at this pride indoctrination. I’m not trying to be mean, but who made this logo? They got all the rainbow mafia colors, and it looks like a p-nis," Flores said, holding up a design made by a local school. The image depicts a tree on top of a hill, illustrated in rainbow colors. "Like literally that’s where we’re at. So, I’m sorry that’s f---ing cracked out. If your child is in public school, please remove them because they’re going to be gay and r-tarded. Thank you, Santa Rosa schools," Flores said. Flores' criticisms, usually couched in similar language, cut across both parties. "Every day my Instagram algorithm is filled with reels of Democrats and Republicans arguing back and forth deciding who is more gay and r-tarded even though they are two sides of the same bird [sic]," Flores said. LOS ANGELES SCHOOLS QUIETLY REMOVE COMPULSORY 'AFFIRM AND RESPECT' GENDER IDENTITY PLEDGE FROM LGBTQ TRAINING "The real puppet master, as always, the Freemasons. This is not a conspiracy. And that is who is pulling the narrative of both sides — red and blue." Flores recounted that she was once a government employee but was forced out of the role and is banned from serving in public roles again. "I got started in my activism because I am a former government employee. I’m a whistleblower who was forced out of the government." Flores said she was removed over COVID-19 mask mandates and the information that was being shared with parents. For his own part, Jones has centered his campaign around issues like affordability, government transparency and protecting government-run programs. On his website, Jones has listed three main priorities: ending corruption, lowering the cost of living and resource sustainability in government. His stances have attracted endorsements from progressive groups like Indivisible and Our Revolution, organizations with ties to progressive Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt. Throughout his campaign, Jones has highlighted his family’s struggle with financial stability. He grew up in a military family and had a disabled father. According to Jones, the family also struggled to overcome medical debt, relying on Medicaid and food stamps. In her endorsement of Jones, which she made shortly after the resignation of Rep. Eric Swalwell, D-Calif., Flores praised Jones’ promise to be a voice for survivors of sexual misconduct. Swalwell, a prominent California Democrat, surrendered his office after several women accused him of unwanted sexual advances, allegations that he denied. WASHINGTON MOTHER PULLS CHILDREN FROM SCHOOL AFTER PRIDE LESSON SHOWN IN MUSIC CLASS WITHOUT NOTICE "Thank you for being one of the only candidates — and this is insane because you’re not even in office yet, but you’re talking about this very critical issue, so God bless you, brother," Flores said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP After Fox News Digital reached out to Flores, who has over 144,000 followers on Instagram, for comment, she posted a video response on Instagram dismissing the inquiry and saying she was a "private citizen" and that her social media accounts are "not monetized." "My views are mine & mine alone. I am an unpaid advocate & have never been paid to support a political candidate," her post said. "I am highly against the two-party system. If I feel someone is a good fit for office, I support them. F--- your gangs! It’s really that simple!"

articles.summary: James Talarico’s lead over Ken Paxton has fallen by one point according to two new polls, with fewer undecided voters left.
articles.body:
James Talarico's poll lead over Ken Paxton in the crunch Texas Senate battle has fallen by one point according to two new opinion polls, which also showed the number of undecided Texan voters has been reduced.

Democrats are hoping to win control of the Senate at the November midterms and victory in Texas—a traditional Republican stronghold that last elected a Democratic senator in 1988—would significantly boost their chances.

Friday saw the publication of the latest Texas Public Opinion Research survey which polled 1,007 likely Texan voters between September 19 and 22. The poll, which had a 3.6 percent margin of error, found state Representative Talarico leading current Texas Attorney General Paxton by five points with 49 percent of the vote against 44 percent.

The last Texas Public Opinion Research survey , of 1,000 likely Texas voters conducted from August 21-24, gave Talarico a six-point lead, with 48 percent of the vote against Paxton's 42 percent.

Notably the proportion of undecided voters has also fallen from seven percent in August to three percent this month, with Libertarian candidate Ted Brown also gaining two percentage points. However, the decrease in Talarico's support remains within the margin of error.

Separately a new Texas Southern University survey gave Talarico a lead of just one point, with 47 percent of the vote against 46 percent for Paxton and three percent for Brown. This survey of 1,800 Texan likely voters took place between September 15 and 19 and has a 2.31 percent margin of error.

By contrast in the previous Texas Southern University poll Talarico was ahead by two percentage points, on 47 percent to Paxton's 45 percent with another two percent for Brown. For this, 1,200 likely Texan voters were surveyed over July 27 and July 30. Once again however, the one percent decrease in Talarico's lead is less than the margin of error. Over the same period the proportion of undecided voters fell from six percent to four percent.

Newsweek contacted the Talarico and Paxton senate campaigns for comment via email on Saturday outside of regular office hours.

Talarico leads Paxton according to eight different pollsters , though several are within the margin of error, and thus too close to call.

An Emerson College survey , conducted September 12-14, gave Talarico a 1-point lead with 47 percent of the vote to Paxton's 46 percent. The poll surveyed 1,000 voters with a margin of error of 3 percentage points.

Between August 30 and September 1, AARP surveyed 895 likely voters, giving Talarico a 4-point lead with a 3.3-point margin of error. Similarly, a YouGov/Univision poll of 1,000 registered voters that took place between August 27 and September 4 put Talarico ahead by 5 points, with a 3.6-point margin of error.

On Thursday, Talarico challenged Paxton to a televised debate on Fox News during an appearance at the Texas Tribune Festival in Austin.

He accused Paxton of "dodging debates all year" continuing: "So let's go to Ken Paxton's safe space. Let's do Bret Baier on Fox News . I'll go into the lions den."

According to Federal Election Commission (FEC) figures up to June 30 the official Talarico senate campaign raised $31,853,507, significantly ahead of the Paxton campaign on $9,147,100.

The FED data showed 45 percent of donations to Talarico's campaign came from out of state, with California being the biggest contributor, compared with 17.1 percent for Paxton.

Contact Newsweek editor on this story: Edward Pearcey.

articles.title: Hidden California desert pet cemetery holds unexpected piece of White House history
articles.summary: Charley Stewart's Haven for Pets in Desert Hot Springs holds graves of Gerald Ford's dog Liberty and pets once owned by Liberace and Hollywood stars.
articles.body: When members of the Secret Service swarmed Charley Stewart’s plot of land in the middle of California's Sonoran Desert, he wasn’t confused or worried — he knew what they had come for. "They have representatives, the Secret Service, and the secretaries, and all those people come by," he told Fox News Digital. "It’s like a circus." Stewart owns and operates Haven for Pets, a pet cemetery in Desert Hot Springs. When one of the nation’s most famous dogs — former President Gerald Ford’s golden retriever, Liberty — was set to be buried there, Secret Service agents visited the cemetery to inspect the grounds ahead of the burial, Stewart said. DISCOVERIES THAT RESHAPED WHAT HISTORIANS KNEW ABOUT AMERICA'S FOUNDING FATHERS "Before she got buried out there, the Secret Service had to go out and look for mines and walk around," said the cemetery owner. "I mean, Gerald Ford was the President of the United States." The female golden retriever arrived at the White House as a puppy and became the nation’s first dog, later giving birth to nine puppies in 1975 on the third floor of the White House. Liberty was the first dog to give birth in the White House. The frequently photographed canine enjoyed the White House life. She posed on the North Lawn, lounged beside the commander in chief in the Oval Office, swam in the pool at Camp David and even received fan mail from Americans across the country. The Fords kept one of Liberty’s puppies, a female named Misty, who is buried alongside her mother at Haven for Pets. Their grave sites leave an unexpected piece of presidential history tucked away in Stewart’s pet cemetery. RONALD REAGAN'S GRANDDAUGHTER, KEVIN MCCARTHY HONOR LATE PRESIDENT'S LEGACY ON HIS 115TH BIRTHDAY Stewart’s Haven for Pets dates back to the 1960s. It opened as an extension of a full-service Palm Springs kennel called Dogtown USA, which was known for providing grooming services to celebrity pets. Dogtown was purchased by Stewart’s father, Charles Stewart, in 1959, and Stewart recalled the story of how the pet cemetery came to be. "My father told me a story one time — he went over to talk to some people and their dog had died, and they threw it in a garbage can, and the head was hanging out," Stewart said. "From that horrible sight, my father said, ‘We’ve got to take care of these babies.’ And so he decided to do that." "It took a couple years to do the paperwork, but that’s what he did … This was an input my father never got over," he added. Haven for Pets’ celebrity canine clientele extends beyond the White House, all the way to Hollywood. STAGECOACH FESTIVALGOERS SPLIT ON WHETHER AMERICA IS HEADED IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION AHEAD OF ITS 250TH BIRTHDAY World-famous pianist Liberace has six of his dogs buried in the cemetery, under headstones that list their owner as "Lee," his nickname. Actor Michael Landon and Academy Award-winning composer Jimmy Van Heusen also have their pets buried there. Stewart told Fox News Digital the VIP connections grew out of his family’s work caring for pets belonging to celebrities who lived in the Coachella Valley. "Going back to Leonard Firestone and the Marx Brothers down here in Thunderbird Country Club, my dad would take care of their dogs," he shared. "We’d groom them and we boarded them … We did business with them." Roughly 1,000 pets are buried in the cemetery. In its early days decades ago, the burial rate was $35. These days it costs nearly $900. Stewart said that, at one point, the cemetery would handle five burials a week, but the figure has fallen to three or four a year because he wants to limit the frequency of burials and extend the life of the cemetery grounds. 1,000-YEAR-OLD CHURCH MYSTERY CRACKED BY STUDENTS FROM KING CHARLES' ALMA MATER Stewart told Fox News Digital the unadvertised cemetery is not easy to find — and he intends to keep it that way. "I don’t advertise the cemetery, it’s all word of mouth," he said. "I don’t want to speed up the process. The cemetery right now is set up in a way that it’s going to last way in excess of 200 years." articles.title: US, China strike deal to lower tariffs on $30B in goods after Trump-Xi Washington summit
articles.summary: The United States and China agreed to slash tariffs on $30 billion in goods after Trump and Xi Jinping's three-day Washington summit this week.
articles.body: The United States and China agreed to lower tariffs on $30 billion worth of goods traded between the two countries following a three-day summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C. According to the White House, the $30 billion in reciprocal tariff reductions apply to "non-sensitive goods." U.S. exports including agricultural products, fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices will receive favorable tariff treatment in China. Meanwhile, U.S. imports of Chinese-made small appliances, toys, holiday decorations and children's car seats will also receive preferential treatment. The agreement was reached through the U.S.-China Board of Trade, a body first proposed during Trump's visit to China in May and formally established during Xi's visit to Washington this week. XI PRAISES US STATE VISIT 'PERFECTION' AS TRUMP CALLS MEETINGS 'VERY PRODUCTIVE' U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that "a lot more details" about the new trade agreement will be released on Monday. Greer said the tariff terms were hammered out after weeks of negotiations. Neither country has released the final tariff rates or all the products that will receive favored status going forward. This marks one of the most significant cooldowns in the trade war Trump launched against China in February 2025, when he levied a 10% tariff on all Chinese imports, citing Beijing's alleged role in the fentanyl crisis and illegal immigration. China hit back with levies on U.S. coal, liquefied natural gas, crude oil and cars. BESSENT REVEALS EXTENSION TO BUSAN AGREEMENT WITH CHINA UNTIL JANUARY At their peak, U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods reached a staggering 145% in April 2025, shortly after Trump unveiled his "Liberation Day" reciprocal tariffs. China responded with tariffs of up to 125% on U.S. goods. U.S. and Chinese negotiators met in Geneva in May 2025 and agreed to a 90-day truce that lowered U.S. tariffs to 30% and China's to 10%. The agreement was extended for another 90 days in August. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Trump and Xi reached another tentative agreement during talks in South Korea in October 2025. Under the deal, China agreed to crack down on fentanyl precursors, resume purchases of U.S. soybeans and ease restrictions on rare-earth exports, while the United States agreed to further ease tariffs. The two countries will now use the Board of Trade to negotiate additional tariff reductions and other trade disputes, leaving open the possibility of broader agreements in the months ahead.

articles.title: Trump blocks CNN from traveling on Air Force One
articles.summary: CNN was slated to cover the president on Saturday on behalf of the television pool, but White House guidance did not include CNN in its traveling list.
articles.body:
In President Donald Trump 's latest move to restrict certain news outlets' access, CNN was not permitted to join the president on Air Force One on Saturday, Sept. 26, as he traveled to a football game at the University of Tennessee.

"I want real news. I love an open, free press," Trump said Saturday morning to reporters when asked about the decision to bar CNN. "What I don't like is the fake press, where a group like CNN, with few people watching, or MSDNC," the name that he calls MS NOW, formerly MSNBC.

CNN anchor Anderson Cooper announced the news about the Air Force One decision on his show Friday night. CNN was slated to cover Trump on Saturday on behalf of the television pool – where ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and FOX take turns covering Trump and sharing camera feeds with the other networks. CNN White House correspondent Alayna Treene explained to Cooper that the White House's guidance for the next day was released and that CNN was not included on the list of outlets traveling with Trump.

"The White House is barring CNN from flying on Air Force One on Saturday as part of the news outlet's duties covering the president on behalf of major television networks," CNN Chief White House Correspondent Kaitlan Collins said in a post on X.

Networks halt White House pool after Trump bars outlets

A CNN broadcast tent sits vacant at the White House grounds after US President Donald Trump banned three major news outlets, CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, in Washington, DC. on Sept. 21, 2026. Major television networks suspended their White House pool coverage and will no longer send camera crews to cover President Donald Trump's pool events, standing in solidarity with CNN after Trump denied White House access to reporters of three outlets. The move from the five networks that make up the television pool ‒ ABC, CBS, NBC and Fox News, in addition to CNN ‒ means a broadcast television feed that is distributed widely for media won't be carried for most of Trump's events.

The latest action comes amid a legal dispute after the president attempted to block three news outlets – CNN, MS NOW and Politico – from the White House. Here's the timeline:

Sept. 18: Trump announced on Truth Social that the three networks were banned from the White House .

Sept. 19: Journalists from those outlets attempted to enter the White House but were denied entry, and their press credential were taken by Secret Service.

Sept. 21: The networks filed a lawsuit against Trump and three White House officials.

Sept. 23: On the first day of Trump's U.S.-China Summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the primary television pool did not cover the president as they stood in solidarity with CNN. Chinese state media and other non-television American outlets did cover the summit.

Sept. 24: Shortly after midnight, a U.S. federal judge ordered that the ban be lifted for two weeks .

Sept. 24: Shortly after noon, journalists from those networks were able to access White House grounds and recover their confiscated passes.

Sept. 25: Television pool cameras covered the second day of Trump and Xi's summit, including a trip to the National Archives to show off documents , including the Constitution, which establishes a free press in its First Amendment.

Sept. 25: The White House releases travel guidance for Saturday, Sept. 26, that does not include CNN.

Trump spent his morning doubling down on his ban, saying in a Truth Social post that "FAKE NEWS SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED IN THE WHITE HOUSE!!! IT HAS GONE ON FAR TOO LONG, AT A TREMENDOUS COST TO OUR COUNTRY."

"Why should perpetrators of FAKE NEWS, like CNN and MSDNC, be allowed access to a very sacred place, the White House? Despite my big Election Win, almost 100% of "TRUMP" coverage is negative, and has been for years," Trump said in a second Sept. 26 post .

articles.title: Kumaraswamy to Election Commission: Tell the truth, protect your own dignity
articles.summary: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy urged the Election Commission to disclose the truth amid reported internal friction, and accused Congress and Rahul Gandhi of politicising it.

Congress, he said, rushed to cry foul without giving the constitutional body room to explain itself, and such conduct only chips away at public faith in the electoral process.The Union minister went further, accusing Congress of making a habit of targeting constitutional bodies whenever the party’s own failures on the political or administrative front come under scrutiny. articles.title: Venezuelan government, opposition agree to work towards reform of top court
articles.summary: The two sides appointed a committee to review selection of candidates for Supreme Court of Justice.
articles.body:
Venezuela’s interim government has concluded a second round of talks with the political opposition, reaching an agreement to work towards reforming Venezuela’s top court.

The deal was announced on Friday and represents the first tangible step towards judicial reforms promised by interim President Delcy Rodriguez.

Both sides said in a joint statement that they had appointed a seven-member panel to review the system used to select candidates for the court and agreed to “continue the analysis and review of legislative instruments needed for the transformation of the judicial system”.

The government side was led by National Assembly chief Jorge Rodriguez, while the opposition was represented by Dinorah Figuera, who led the opposition bloc that won Venezuela’s last internationally recognised election in 2015.

Venezuela’s interim government, which took power after the US military abducted former President Nicolas Maduro in January, has brought the country into closer alignment with the US but has been slow to deliver on promises to open up the political system.

Critics have compared the arrangement, which has included a deal granting the US control over large parts of Venezuela’s oil reserves , to those previously imposed on oil-rich nations by colonial powers such as Great Britain.

Rights groups say that the repressive apparatus of the Maduro era has also remained in place, despite promises of change from the new government.

Rodriguez promised elections during her speech at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) this week but offered no firm timeline.

US President Donald Trump and Rodriguez met on the sidelines of UNGA, her first visit to the US since the abduction of her predecessor. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that Trump and Rodriguez discussed restructuring billions of dollars in Venezuela’s sovereign debt.

Trump said on Friday that he spoke with Rodriguez about elections in the past week, but offered no further details.

“I did,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “I spoke about elections.”

The government and the opposition held an initial round of talks in August, when they agreed to overhaul the judicial system and win back Venezuelan assets frozen by the Bank of England.

The next round of talks is scheduled next month.

articles.title: Cruz says winning AI race against China is 'single most important economic question' for America
articles.summary: Ted Cruz claims China and "effective altruism" backers are waging a deliberate influence campaign to shape AI policy and data center debates.
articles.body: America's AI race against China, which has become a major point of debate as midterms approach, is a race filled with "coordinated" propaganda, warned Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas. In recent months, data centers and AI policy have been debated in Congress and at the kitchen tables of American families. But Cruz, who chairs the Senate Commerce Committee, told Fox News Digital that much of the new opposition to data centers is being manipulated by a well-funded and coordinated campaign. "It's the same reason we saw Middle Eastern countries paying for anti-fracking movements," Cruz said. "Because if they can convince America, 'Don't develop your oil and gas, just buy it from us,' well, that's great for them and terrible for us. The same is true on data centers. If they can convince Americans, 'You don't want data centers here, you want to just rely on the Chinese for AI,' that's great for China, and it's terrible for America." CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE Direct funding from the Chinese government into the U.S. on data center policies has not been revealed. However, in June, OpenAI announced it had banned ChatGPT accounts believed to have originated in China, and said that the accounts were generating social media comments and images alleging that data centers are raising electricity costs for Americans. OpenAI said in a statement that it shut down "two clusters of ChatGPT accounts likely originating from China that [OpenAI] banned after they used our models in support of apparent covert influence operations that promoted narratives in an attempt to manipulate a legitimate debate about American AI and wider tech policies." Cruz called the effort to craft policy to ensure the U.S. wins the AI race is "the single most important economic question facing America today." INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE' "If China wins, AI will be focused on espionage and propaganda and control and surveillance, because that's the Chinese Communist Party," Cruz said. "It will be their values. They will use AI to try to control you. If America wins, I want American values to be reflected in AI. I want free speech and individualism and free enterprise and privacy to be reflected in AI, not control and power." Cruz called opposition to AI advancement and data centers the "dominant position on the Democratic side." The third-term Republican said the Democrats' position is aligned with that of big industry players including Anthropic that he said want exemption from antitrust laws and to "get in bed with government" to control AI development. THE HIDDEN LEFT-WING NETWORK POWERING A ‘CONSERVATIVE’ REBELLION AGAINST A MAJOR TRUMP PRIORITY Cruz associated this position with leftist ideology and the emerging tech philosophy known as "effective altruism." "These folks from effective altruism are all hardcore leftists, and they want to use AI to push their leftist ideology," Cruz said. "Part of what we're seeing is a money grab, where there's an old concept in economics called rent seeking, which is big companies typically go to government and say, 'Give me a benefit, entrench me.' We’re seeing the giant AI companies going to government saying, 'Hey, why don't you put us in charge of government and let's set the rules so no one could compete with us.'" Parker Thayer, an investigative researcher at Capital Research Center in Washington, D.C., told Fox News Digital last week that effective altruism is associated with what he called the "AI doomerism movement." Facebook co-founder and billionaire Democratic mega-donor Dustin Moskovitz and his wife Cari Tuna have been leading financial backers of organizations associated with the effective altruism movement. Moskovitz left Facebook in 2008. The couple founded Coefficient Giving, formerly known as Open Philanthropy, and remains its "main funders," according to the organization. Tuna serves as its president. Coefficient Giving says its artificial intelligence work has expanded rapidly, with $168 million committed to AI safety, security and field-building in 2024 and $351 million in 2025. The organization says it is on track to commit more than $1 billion to AI policy advocacy in 2026. In a 2021 grant application description, the organization said it seeks "to fund programs and events in a variety of areas of interest to Coefficient Giving — including effective altruism, global catastrophic risks, biosecurity, AI for epistemics, forecasting, and other areas." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In 2015, Coefficient Giving launched "Project Tailwind," an initiative where the Moskovitz-funded organization issued a "call for founders to launch ambitious AI safety initiatives."

articles.title: Cuba condemns US ‘collective punishment’ as Trump predicts deal
articles.summary: The Cuban foreign minister’s comments come days after the US told the UN that ‘freedom will be coming’ to the country.
articles.body:
Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez has condemned the United States’s oil blockade against his country during his speech at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), calling it an “act of collective punishment” intended to trigger a humanitarian crisis.

His comments on Saturday come as tensions between Washington and Havana remain high and as US President Donald Trump predicted that the two countries would reach an agreement, while saying he did not believe military action would be necessary.

“I would say that Cuba and us will make a deal,” Trump told reporters at the White House on Saturday. “I don’t think we’ll need the military. Cuba is failing very badly. We want to help Cuba.”

In his UNGA speech, Rodriguez said Havana remained open to negotiations.

“We have always been and will always be prepared for dialogue with the government of the United States in order to try to find solutions to the various bilateral differences that we have,” he said, adding that talks would have to be based on “sovereign equality” and take place “without preconditions”.

Rodriguez also addressed the possibility of US military action, saying it would cause huge destruction.

“Let’s hope that this never happens,” he said.

Earlier this week, Trump called Cuba an “absolutely failed state” during his own UN address and said “freedom will be coming” to the island. Cuba’s delegation walked out during the speech.

The US has maintained an economic embargo on Cuba for more than 60 years. The Trump administration has previously said that it wants a change in Cuba’s government. Since earlier this year, the US has additionally imposed an oil blockade that has put the country under severe pressure, dealing with fuel shortages and ongoing blackouts. Cuban officials have also blamed it on problems providing food and other basic needs for its population.

The measures have drawn criticism from countries including Brazil, Mexico and Pakistan, which have called for an end to the embargo and new oil blockade and opposed unilateral economic restrictions on Cuba.

Since 1992, the UN General Assembly has overwhelmingly backed an annual resolution calling for an end to the US economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba.

articles.title: Trump rejects combining US-China AI efforts
articles.summary: The US president said the fears over AI were just ‘hoaxes’.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has said the country will not be heeding growing calls to regulate the development of artificial intelligence.

On Saturday, as he departed the White House, Trump told reporters the US “is not going to be putting on brakes” for AI, even as US lawmakers and CEOs of some of the nation’s largest tech firms agreed on the need to slow its pace, citing its potential to put humanity at risk.

The president likened those fears to other issues he has previously claimed are “hoaxes”, including climate change and the investigation that examined whether his 2016 campaign colluded with Russian operatives.

“When they wanna put on brakes, it’s just like everybody’s going to be dead. You’re all supposed to be dead now, because of global warming. It’s like Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. All of these different hoaxes,” Trump said.

“What they wanna do is stop our progress, because we’re leading China by a lot,” he added. “And we’re going to keep it that way.”

Trump, who just concluded a 3-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said the US should not cooperate with China on the technology.

“I would rather not integrate, because we’re leading by a lot,” he said. “When you’re leading, you don’t open it up to each other.”

During his final address before the United Nations General Assembly, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged leaders on Tuesday to enact guardrails on AI, warning that unchecked development “without accountability” could put the world at risk.

US lawmakers and experts had hoped Trump and Xi would use their meeting to deliver a breakthrough agreement on AI. But that did not materialise.

“We didn’t spend that much time talking about it,” Trump said.

As criticism rippled through Washington — and around the world — over the squandered opportunity, the White House on Friday said the US and China agreed to establish a “bilateral communication channel” for AI incidents. There was no immediate comment from Beijing on the White House statement.

The president, however, indicated that any AI discussions he had with Xi, who is set to meet with Trump two more times this year, largely focused on his preferred name for the technology: “super intelligence”.

China “respects” Washington’s switch in phrasing from artificial intelligence to “super intelligence”, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Saturday, after Donald Trump said Xi appeared to like the rewording.

The US president announced on Tuesday that his administration would rename AI as “super intelligence”, or SI, in official communications.

“Artificial intelligence technologies are continuously developing, all parties can strengthen exchanges, discuss in-depth and seek consensus in light of the latest situation,” said a statement from an unidentified Chinese ministry spokesperson.

When it comes to AI, Xi has taken a more measured tone than Trump and said the technology must develop under human control.

articles.title: Trump's home county hits pause on data centers over environment and electric bill concerns
articles.summary: Palm Beach County passed a one-year moratorium on data centers amid concerns over environmental impact, noise pollution, and rising electric bills.
articles.body: Palm Beach County — home to President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago — passed a one-year moratoriam on the planning and construction of data centers as commissioners seek to conduct a thorough review of data centers’ impacts on the environment, noise pollution, and electric bills. The moratorium, passed on Thursday, comes just weeks after Trump said that communities that reject data centers would "end up being backwards and poor." Among the wealthiest counties in the country, Palm Beach County includes the town of Palm Beach, home to 65 billionaires. "If you want to go through poverty, crime and squalor, I would say don’t approve of data centers," Trump said from the Oval Office on Sep. 4. The Palm Beach County Commissioners’ 6-0 vote doesn’t put a permanent ban on data centers. Instead, it gives county leadership time to conduct environmental impact reviews before updating zoning rules for where data centers can be built. TRUMP’S DATA CENTER PUSH FRACTURES CONGRESS AS LOCAL ANGER EXPLODES: 'GRASPING AT STRAWS' The moratorium applies to all new applications for data centers with an anticipated peak electrical load of at least 50 megawatts. "Many communities want the economic benefits a data center brings, but we all fear the higher power bills, the negative environmental impact, disruptive noise, the depletion of water resources," a Palm Beach County resident shared during Thursday’s meeting. Trump has made expanding data centers and accelerating artificial intelligence a cornerstone of his agenda, arguing that the United States cannot afford to lose the AI race to China and warning that opposition to data centers only benefits Beijing. Data centers are the physical backbone of artificial intelligence, housing thousands of powerful computers that store and process digital information while providing the computing power needed to train and run AI systems. Palm Beach County has already approved in 2016 the construction of "Project Tango" — a proposed 202-acre AI data center, which is located 20 miles from Mar-a-Lago. The data center will also be built near an elementary school and homes. FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS QUESTION WHETHER AI’S PROMISE OUTWEIGHS ITS RISKS In July, commissioners voted 6-1 to reject a proposal to expand Project Tango by roughly 1.67 million square feet. But existing approvals for two 100,000-square-foot data center buildings remain in place. Residents at the Thursday meeting said Project Tango was the driving factor behind the push to hit pause on data center project approvals, with several residents advocating for no data centers to be built. articles.title: Democrats now have easier paths to flipping the Senate. Here are races to watch.
articles.summary: Democrats’ chances of flipping the Senate have grown in recent months as President Donald Trump’s unpopularity, as well as frustration with the economy, push...
articles.body:
Democrats now have easier paths to flipping the Senate. Here are races to watch.

Democrats' chances of flipping the Senate have grown in recent months as President Donald Trump's unpopularity, as well as frustration with the economy, push voters away from Republicans.

Democrats have been favored to seize control of the House, which has a narrow Republican majority. The math in the Senate is more daunting: Democrats control 47 seats to Republicans' 53.

The clearest path to a majority requires Democrats to retain all of their seats and win four GOP-controlled seats, including at least two in states President Donald Trump won by double digits in 2024. That path, which once felt like a long shot, now seems feasible.

A Wednesday update from the Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan election analysis site, described control of the Senate as "a true coin flip, with viable paths for both parties to win or keep a majority." Some other analysts have concluded the map is even more favorable to Democrats.

The political environment has shifted enough in recent months that some Republicans have suggested that the GOP should scale back spending in Georgia and North Carolina, where Trump won in 2024 but the party's nominees have lagged in polls.

Here are the races to watch as the battle for the Senate grows increasingly competitive.

The races moving toward Democrats: Georgia, Iowa, Texas, Kansas, South Carolina

Sen. Jon Ossoff is now heavily favored to win reelection in Georgia in a race which Cook rates as "Likely Democratic." Republicans initially viewed the race as one of their leading opportunities to gain a seat, but controversies involving the GOP nominee, Rep. Mike Collins, have helped Ossoff pull away.

Iowa and Texas, two states that backed Trump by a double-digit margin in 2024, are now in the toss-up column.

James Talarico, a state representative, has led Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in many polls as he tries to become the first Democrat to win a statewide election in Texas this century. After Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn in the Republican primary, the race exploded into an expensive, high-profile contest. Scandals have eroded Paxton's popularity, while Democrats hope that Talarico's faith-based politics has broad appeal and can overcome criticism that he's too socially liberal.

Josh Turek, an Iowa state representative and former Paralympic athlete, is tapping voters' frustrations with the effects of Trump's tariffs to try to win crossover support. He faces Rep. Ashley Hinson, a former television anchor viewed by national Republicans as a strong candidate, for the seat being vacated by retiring Republican Joni Ernst.

Kansas, a state which Trump won by 16 percentage points in 2024, has emerged as a surprising Democratic target in recent months. Although incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall is still favored, the challenge from Adam Hamilton, a political outsider and prominent pastor, has concerned some Republicans.

In South Carolina, Republican Sen. Darline Graham, who was appointed after her brother, Lindsey Graham, died in July, is favored to defeat Democratic pediatrician Annie Andrews. Graham's weaknesses include a lack of political experience and skepticism about her right-wing credentials from some conservatives who preferred her opponents in the Republican primary.

The one race shifting toward Republicans: New Hampshire

New Hampshire, a state Kamala Harris won in 2024, is one of Republicans' best chances of flipping a Democratic seat. Polls have shown a close race between Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas and Republican John Sununu, who served in the Senate from 2003 to 2009 and is the son of former governor John H. Sununu and brother to popular former governor Chris Sununu. They are competing to succeed retiring Sen. Jeanne Shaheen (D).

Republicans plan to spend heavily in the state to support Sununu, who has distanced himself from Trump.

The other battlegrounds: North Carolina, Alaska, Maine, Michigan, Ohio

Michigan's race presents another opportunity for Republicans to flip a Democratic-controlled seat, as Republicans have criticized the Democratic nominee, Abdul El-Sayed, as being too far to the left. El-Sayed has sought to unify Michigan Democrats since winning a bruising primary against Rep. Haley Stevens. A recent Washington Post-Schar School poll showed him with a narrow edge but lagging the Democratic nominee for governor among Black voters, independents and voters who say they are unwilling to support a Muslim for president.

Republicans describe their nominee, former eight-term congressman Mike Rogers, as a formidable candidate who narrowly lost a 2024 campaign for Senate. Democrats have sought to tie him to Trump, whose popularity remains low in the state.

In North Carolina, Gov. Roy Cooper, a popular Democrat, is favored over former Republican National Committee chair Michael Whatley in a race that looks to be Democrats' likeliest flip. The swing state's race has been a top target of Democrats since incumbent Sen. Thom Tillis (R) announced his retirement in 2025. Both parties have spent heavily on the race, but Cooper has consistently led in public polling.

In Alaska, Democrats are hopeful that former congresswoman Mary Peltola, a moderate, can oust Sen. Dan S. Sullivan (R). Peltola's path to victory in the deep red state might rely upon frustration with high diesel prices and the presence of three other Republicans, including retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan, on the state's ranked-choice election ballot.

Maine's race has undergone a significant shake-up in recent months after former nominee Graham Platner withdrew following an allegation of sexual assault. Troy Jackson, a progressive logger and former state Senate president who was nominated to replace Platner at a convention, is hoping to unseat longtime Sen. Susan Collins (R), who has long cultivated a moderate image to garner crossover support.

In Ohio, former longtime senator Sherrod Brown (D) faces Republican incumbent Sen. Jon Husted, who was appointed in 2025 after his predecessor, JD Vance, became vice president. Although Brown lost reelection by four percentage points in 2024 while Trump won the state by a double-digit margin, analysts believe that Trump's lagging popularity could fuel Brown's comeback.

The reach states: Minnesota and Nebraska

Cook rates Democrats and Republicans, respectively, as "likely" to hold their seats in Minnesota and Nebraska, but their victories are not assured.

In Nebraska, independent Dan Osborn, a union leader who says he would not caucus with either Democrats or Republicans in the Senate, faces Sen. Pete Ricketts (R), the son of billionaire TD Ameritrade founder Joe Ricketts. Osborn ran for Senate in 2024 and overperformed in losing by seven percentage points while Trump won by 20 percentage points. Democrats are not fielding a candidate, and the state party endorsed Osborn.

Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan (D) faces former football journalist Michele Tafoya, a Republican, in a state Harris won by four percentage points. Flanagan defeated a more moderate candidate in a bruising primary. Republicans hope that voters unhappy with the outgoing Democratic governor, Tim Walz, will punish Flanagan and that Tafoya will benefit from her high-profile career as a sideline reporter.

CORRECTION: A previous version of this article incorrectly said that Republican Mike Rogers outperformed Donald Trump when he narrowly lost the Michigan Senate race in 2024. Trump won Michigan in the presidential election that year.

Theodoric Meyer contributed reporting to this article.

articles.title: China, US agree to AI dialogue, tariff cuts on $30 billion in goods during Xi visit
articles.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 26 () - The United States and China have agreed to reduce tariffs on $30 billion of goods and launch a dialogue on AI, both countries said fol...
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping meet at the White House

SHANGHAI, Sept 26 (Reuters) - The United States and China have agreed to reduce tariffs on $30 billion of goods and launch a dialogue on AI, both countries said following President Xi ‌Jinping's visit to Washington.

The tariff reductions would apply to US exports such as agricultural goods, wood ‌and cosmetics, as well as US imports including small appliances, toys, decorations, a White House statement said on Friday.

"The two countries reached ​consensus on recommendations for more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction," the White House said.

The three-day summit between Xi and President Donald Trump, which ended on Friday, showcased personal diplomacy rather than big public breakthroughs. Xi has since landed in Beijing, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported on Saturday.

The two sides ‌also agreed to set up a trade ⁠council and extend the outcomes of earlier talks in Kuala Lumpur, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said.

The agreement follows a move by the world's two largest economies to extend by ⁠two months a trade truce that had been due to expire on November 10, allowing more time to work on a potentially bigger trade deal, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Wednesday.

"This historic visit enriched the constructive ​and stable ​China-US relationship, upheld the overall stability of bilateral ties, ​opened a new chapter in China-US relations, and ‌will have a far-reaching impact on world peace and development," Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said in a statement.

On artificial intelligence, the two sides agreed to hold a dialogue on the technology's risks and benefits, with the next round of discussions set for November, and to set up a communication channel for AI-related incidents, the Chinese Foreign Ministry and the White House said.

The White House said that the leaders had agreed ‌to use the term "super intelligence" in place of "artificial intelligence."

In a ​separate statement, the Chinese ministry said that Beijing valued Washington's use ​of the new term.

As AI technology continues ​to advance, the two sides should step up exchanges and work toward consensus in ‌line with new developments, it said.

The two sides ​also agreed to support each ​other in hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting and the Group of 20 summit, with both leaders planning to attend the gatherings hosted by the other.

On foreign policy, the leaders agreed ​that Iran should fulfil its commitment not ‌to develop nuclear weapons, and that no country or entity should impose transit tolls on ​international waterways, both countries said.

(Reporting by Shanghai Newsroom and Katharine Jackson in Washington; Editing by ​Christopher Cushing, Gareth Jones, Sergio Non and Sanjeev Miglani)

articles.title: Varun Gandhi’s political revival on cards with Rajya Sabha nomination?
articles.summary: Speculation grows that BJP may nominate sidelined ex-MP Varun Gandhi to Rajya Sabha from UP as 10 seats fall vacant, boosting party’s face vs Congress.
articles.body: Lucknow: More than two years after he was sidelined by the BJP and denied a ticket in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, former party MP Varun Gandhi may be on the cusp of an unexpected political revival.Speculation is growing within political circles that BJP may nominate Varun Gandhi to Rajya Sabha, a move that would enable the party to project a prominent face against Congress, particularly the Gandhi family.A senior BJP functionary affirmed that Varun could be one of the contenders for a Rajya Sabha seat for which elections are slated next month. As many as 10 Rajya Sabha seats from UP are falling vacant on Nov 25. Sources indicate that not just a Rajya Sabha seat but something more could be in store for Varun who, otherwise, has been keeping a low profile for the past two years.The buzz around his possible rehabilitation comes nearly six months after Varun met Prime Minister Narendra Modi along with his family.“I had the privilege of meeting Prime Minister Shri @Narendramodi ji along with my family and receiving his blessings and guidance. Your aura radiates a remarkable sense of paternal affection and protective care. Meeting you further reinforces the conviction that you are a true guardian of the nation and its people,” Varun tweeted on March 17, posting a picture of him and his family meeting Modi.The meeting triggered speculation about whether the BJP-Varun relationship was entering a new phase.He also wished PM Modi on his birthday on Sept 17, saying: “A life dedicated to the service of the nation. A day to express our collective gratitude. #HappyBdayPMModi ji”.Varun had fallen out of BJP’s favour after he started consistently and publicly criticising BJP and Modi govt between late 2021 and 2023 over a wide range of economic, agrarian and administrative policies. Rather than a standard political opposition, his criticism was largely delivered through veiled salvos on social media, critical columns and public addresses in his constituency of Pilibhit.BJP sources recalled how Gandhi openly empathised with the farmers who were protesting against the three controversial agri-laws. On Oct 21, 2021, he shared a vintage video of former PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee warning against the “repression” of farmers as a lesson for the central govt.Following the deaths of protesting farmers in Lakhimpur Kheri on Oct 3, 2021, Varun strongly condemned the incident and demanded action against party colleague and then Union minister Ajay Mishra Teni.Shortly after, BJP removed Varun and his mother, Maneka Gandhi, from the party’s national executive committee.Following more than a year of intense protests by farming unions at Delhi’s borders, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a surprise announcement on Nov 19, 2021, declaring that govt would repeal the three legislations.Varun also turned highly critical of Modi govt over the issue of employment, Agnipath scheme and contractual jobs, saying that they could be terminated arbitrarily, leaving youth vulnerable.When PM targeted opposition parties for offering electoral freebies, Varun publicly challenged this stance on X. He questioned why govt expected a “thank you” for giving 5 kg of free ration to the poor while simultaneously writing off Rs 10 lakh crore in bad loans for corrupt corporate defaulters over five years.Varun was subsequently denied a ticket to contest from Pilibhit, the constituency which he had won twice -- first in 2009 and then in 2019. BJP, instead, fielded Jatin Prasada, a former Congressman, who eventually defeated his nearest rival, Bhagwat Saran Gangwar of Samajwadi Party, by a margin of over 1.64 lakh votes.According to a few unconfirmed reports, BJP high command offered him the chance to contest from the high-profile Rae Bareli seat against his cousin Rahul Gandhi in 2024. articles.title: Colours, symbols and the battle for political meaning in UP
articles.summary: UP parties ramp up colour politics ahead of 2027 polls as SP’s PDA Rath Yatra sparks debate on blue, saffron and Ambedkar symbols to woo voters.
articles.body: Lucknow: As political parties in Uttar Pradesh gear up for the 2027 assembly elections, colours are increasingly becoming political messages in themselves. From blue and saffron to green, parties are deploying visual symbolism alongside slogans and icons to signal social alliances, cultural positioning and electoral intent.The latest debate was triggered by Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA Rath Yatra, launched from Rae Bareli. Akhilesh flagged off his Rath Yatra from Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s bastion in a luxury bus carrying the slogan, “Jo peedit hai wahi PDA hai.” The vehicle also prominently displayed a portrait of Dr BR Ambedkar and featured a noticeable saffron shade, elements that political observers believe are far from incidental.The PDA slogan, Ambedkar imagery and blue colour palette are being interpreted as signals aimed at Dalit voters. At the same time, the visible saffron tint on the Rath has generated discussion about whether opposition parties are increasingly seeking to engage with religious and cultural narratives that resonate with a broader Hindu electorate.The yatra came days after SP unveiled blue uniforms for its student wing, a move that drew attention because blue has long been associated with Dalit assertion, the legacy of Dr BR Ambedkar and Bahujan Samaj Party.The symbolism was not lost on BSP chief Mayawati, who argued that adopting blue or invoking Ambedkar’s legacy was not enough to represent the interests of Dalits, tribals, backward classes and other marginalised communities. She maintained that genuine commitment to Ambedkarite politics required substantive policy and ideological change rather than symbolic gestures.However, SP’s former MLC Udaiveer Singh said that the party had always followed in the footsteps of those great personalities who have raised their voices against suppressed, deprived and exploited people, and it has nothing to do with the use of colours and symbols.The debate has highlighted how colours have acquired distinct political meanings in Uttar Pradesh over the years. Blue has traditionally been associated with Dalit empowerment and BSP. Saffron has emerged as the dominant political colour of BJP, drawing from broader Hindu cultural and religious symbolism. Green, meanwhile, has long been associated with Rashtriya Lok Dal and now is also used prominently by AIMIM, where it often carries minority outreach symbolism.Political observers note that in Uttar Pradesh’s highly competitive electoral landscape, colours function as immediate visual cues capable of communicating political intent faster than speeches or manifestos. Flags, scarves, campaign vehicles, stage backdrops and even clothing frequently become instruments of political messaging.The timing is significant. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, BSP’s performance saw a dramatic decline. Its vote share fell from 19.42% in 2019 to 9.39%, and the party failed to win a single seat. SP, which fought the election in alliance with Congress as part of the broader INDIA bloc, emerged as the biggest gainer in the state. It secured a record 37 Lok Sabha seats and garnered 33.59% of the vote share, compared to just five seats and 18.11% vote share in 2019.Congress, meanwhile, also registered significant gains. Contesting as an ally of SP, it increased its vote share from 6.3% in 2019 to 9.53% in 2024 and improved its tally from one seat to six seats. BJP remained the single largest force in the state but also witnessed a decline. Its vote share dropped from 49.98% in 2019 to 41.67% in 2024, while its seat tally came down from 62 to 33 seats.SP functionaries attribute much of their dramatic rise not only to anti-incumbency against BJP but also to a substantial dent in BSP’s traditional support among Jatav Dalits. While some Congress leaders maintain that the shift in Dalit votes was facilitated by SP-Congress alliance, SP camp believes that a section of Jatav voters consciously chose SP in 2024 irrespective of the alliance arrangement.So, since the 2024 LS elections, questions have intensified about the future alignment of Dalit votes in the state. Political parties are now competing not only through policy promises but also through symbols that evoke identity, representation and belonging.Such symbolism is hardly new in Uttar Pradesh politics. BSP’s use of blue, SP’s traditional red-and-green flag, BJP’s saffron imagery and AIMIM’s green branding have all helped create distinct political identities over time. What appears to be changing is parties’ willingness to experiment with colours traditionally associated with rival social or political constituencies.SP functionaries reject suggestions that their use of colours is driven by electoral calculations. They argue that the party’s politics has always focused on the concerns of deprived and marginalised sections of society and that colours should not be overinterpreted. They also reject the claim that the party is borrowing from BJP’s ideological playbook. SP national secretary Avlesh Singh has asserted that the party represents the “true Sanatani” tradition, while accusing BJP leaders of being “pseudo Sanatanis.”UP BJP’s chief spokesperson Dinesh Pratap Singh said people of UP are scared of red colour, used by SP. “Hence the SP Chief first changed the colour of its student’s wing uniform to blue and now putting saffron shade in the rath. Saffron has been and will remain BJP’s colour and 2027 assembly polls will again see saffron wave across the state. Akhilesh these days is so frequently ‘changing colours’ that even the chameleons are embarrassed,” Singh further said.Yet for political observers, the current contest suggests that the battle for Uttar Pradesh in 2027 is likely to be fought not only through caste equations, welfare schemes and political narratives, but also through powerful visual symbols. articles.title: Maher blasts ‘intolerant left’ after Massachusetts lesbian bar faces fury for tweaking COVID-era mask policy
articles.summary: Comedian Bill Maher highlighted the struggling Last Ditch Bar, where lifting a COVID-era mask mandate one night a week sparked firebomb threats.
articles.body: Comedian Bill Maher took aim at his own side of the aisle Friday night, mocking far-left critics who torched a struggling Massachusetts lesbian bar for daring to go mask-optional one night a week. During Friday’s episode of HBO’s "Real Time," Maher weighed in on the viral story regarding Last Ditch Bar and Arts Venue — a lesbian bar in Greenfield, Massachusetts that drew national headlines this week after the Boston Globe reported on a slew of community backlash surrounding the businesses’ decision to lift its COVID-era mask mandate for one night each week. "Here's what's going on at the Last Ditch Bar," Maher said, adding, "It's a very woke bar, which is fine. Their mission statement [is], ‘For dykes, transsexuals, gender freaks, workers and friends.’" NEWSOM'S ADMISSION THAT INFAMOUS COVID MOVE WAS 'INSANE' TRIGGERS VIRAL FURY: 'WE ALL TOLD YOU' "I love the way workers and friends are fourth and fifth on the list," Maher joked. The comedian went on to delve into the bar's financial struggles. The Boston Globe reported that more patrons had said they could not afford the cover charge, and the bar allowed them in anyway. MAHER SKEWERS WEALTHY CELEBS WHO PREACHED 'WE'RE ALL IN IT TOGETHER' DURING COVID AS AMERICANS STRUGGLED "But economically, it wasn't working," Maher said. "Because even though there was a cover charge, if you couldn't pay, they wouldn't make you pay. Homeless, they were welcome in there. Not the cops, but the homeless. But also, it was masked" Maher later pointed out that ‘because they're losing money, one of the owners was living in her truck." BILL MAHER BREAKS WITH THE LEFT TO HAMMER ANTHONY FAUCI AFTER EXPLOSIVE SENATE HEARING In an attempt to keep the doors open, Last Ditch made the decision to lift its strict KN-95 mask mandate one night each week — Saturdays — and allow patrons inside without the COVID-era face coverings, according to the Boston Globe. "It is with love we inform our immunocompromised disabled divas we will be opening Saturday nights as mask optional," Last Ditch wrote in an Aug. 31 Instagram post. ‘COVID 2.0’: LAWMAKERS PUSH BACK ON SWEEPING HEALTH 'POLICE POWER' IN KEY BATTLEGROUND STATE The backlash was swift, with locals flocking to a monthly community meeting on Sept. 11 to air their grievances, the outlet reported. Virtual attendees were quick to criticize the bar owners for their decision, with the meeting taking another turn when some critics objected to a mediator, a licensed therapist who is White. BILL MAHER BLAMES THE FAR-LEFT FOR PUSHING OUT LIBERALS LIKE JOE ROGAN, ELON MUSK OVER TO CONSERVATIVES "A lot of people are calling for an acknowledgment of harm and I’m hearing a WHITE therapist … center[ing] the feelings of a majority white and white adjacent staff," one person said, the newspaper reported. Maher took issue with the far-left bar patrons' apparent lack of understanding of the situation and blasted their intolerance toward the business. BILL MAHER WARNS THAT THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IS BEING 'COLONIZED' BY SOCIALISTS, SAYS HIS 'VOTE IS IN PLAY' "And of course, the tolerant left did what they always do — became very intolerant and left," Maher said. He went on to point to comments reportedly made by critics of the bar. "And statements like, ‘People like you kill disabled people in the name of your own leisure and convenience,’ and ‘I hope your venue gets firebombed.’ This is what I'm talking about. This level of hatred that is out there." Maher's criticism of the political left was noted by NewsBusters Executive Editor Tim Graham, who pointed out what he viewed as hypocrisy on both sides. "This whole story went viral because it's shocking that a mask mandate is still in place at a bar in 2026. I imagine many people can feel more than a hint of the old COVID authoritarianism in the virulent leftist reaction to a single mask-optional night at this establishment," Graham told Fox News Digital. "These same people are probably furious at the Boston Globe for publishing this story. They don't care that the bar was a financial mess." Graham added that Maher seems to have a pet peeve about liberals who preach tolerance but, in Maher's view, fail to practice it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE "Bill Maher has a tendency to go against the dominant grain and can be savage about left-wing intolerance even though he was a massive supporter of Barack Obama," Graham said. "He's been very rough on organized religion, and can bring the pain to other strains of fundamentalism." Fox News Digital reached out to Last Ditch Bar for comment. articles.title: Trump slashes Biden-era fuel economy standards for cars
articles.summary: The new fuel economy standards are the latest assault on Biden-era EV policies.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump announced Saturday that he has approved new fuel economy standards for passenger vehicles, in another move meant to take aim at Biden-era policies supporting electric vehicles.

Trump said in a Truth Social post that he "just approved new Fuel Economy Standards that TERMINATE Sleepy Joe Biden and Pete Boot-EDGE-EDGE's ridiculous EV Mandate. The Dumocrats cost our Great Auto Manufacturers $Billions, forced Americans into cars they never wanted, and wasted Billions on Chargers that were never built."

The announcement comes as the White House faces increased scrutiny for high gas prices — hovering just under $4.50 a gallon on average in the U.S. Saturday — rising car prices and a tough midterm election on the horizon.

"These new Standards will take the waste out of building cars in America. That means LOWER PRICES, saving families thousands on a new, beautiful, and safe car — Far better than the Environmental Monsters that we were building heretofore. Every Manufacturer, from General Motors to Ford to Stellantis, has called me wanting to build here, and now they can!" Trump wrote.

The final rule was not immediately available, and officials from the White House did not immediately respond to questions. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy amplified Trump's post on social media , adding, "A major victory for America's auto workers is COMING MONDAY."

The new regulation is expected to slash fuel economy standards for passenger vehicles by nearly one-third through model year 2031.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's proposed redo of so-called Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards for cars and light-duty trucks would require the sector to average about 34.5 miles per gallon through model year 2031. The rule replaces Biden-era standards, which demanded fleetwide averages of 50.4 mpg.

The revision is one more nail in the coffin for Biden administration electric vehicle incentives.

But experts say its comparatively less important than EPA's move in February to scuttle all climate rules for motor vehicles — including the scientific finding that underpinned them. That's in part because Congress approved language in last year's tax and spending megabill that set aside penalties that carmakers previously paid for failing to meet the fleetwide fuel economy averages.

Joshua Linn, a professor at the University of Maryland, said the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's repeal of noncompliance penalties transformed the CAFE standards into a "suggestion."

"It's like the agency's asking nicely, 'here's where you could be if you added this much technology and made your gasoline cars this much more efficient,'" said Linn, who is also a senior fellow at Resources for the Future. "But there's no penalty if you don't do it."

Whether manufacturers choose to meet those standards or not will now be based on business considerations, not government requirements.

NHTSA's revised standards will almost certainly be challenged in court, as EPA's repeal of vehicle emissions rules and the so-called endangerment finding for greenhouse gases has been.

The courts will decide whether the government can or must require carmakers to improve their fuel economy or invest in electrification. But the rollbacks and Congress' move last year to gut consumer tax incentives for electric vehicles has widened the gap between U.S. transportation policy and global trends favoring EVs.

Dan Becker, director of the Safe Climate Transport Campaign at the Center for Biological Diversity, said the Trump repeals wouldn't do the U.S. car industry any favors.

"This is at a time when the rest of the world is moving to Chinese advanced technology electric vehicles," he said. "So, this essentially says, 'okay, Detroit, you can fail to compete into oblivion.'"

articles.title: Election forecasters don’t see polling ‘sugar-high’ Democrats fear — for now
articles.summary: Pollsters and independent handicappers are increasingly convinced that Democrats aren’t experiencing an artificial “sugar-high” in polling but that multiple metrics are right now pointing to a good midterm environment for the party. The nonpartisan election handicapper Cook Political Report became the latest independent forecaster this week in predicting that Republicans looked poised to lose the…
articles.body:
Pollsters and independent handicappers are increasingly convinced that Democrats aren’t experiencing an artificial “sugar-high” in polling but that multiple metrics are right now pointing to a good midterm environment for the party.

The nonpartisan election handicapper Cook Political Report became the latest independent forecaster this week in predicting that Republicans looked poised to lose the House in November, and recent polling has shown Senate candidates like James Talarico in Texas and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan leading their GOP counterparts.

Decision Desk HQ, too, forecasts a 72 percent probability of Democrats winning the House and a 54 percent probability of the party flipping the Senate.

Experts caution that the dynamics could still change between now and November, noting how Republicans deploy their financial advantage in battleground states remains a key variable.

But they say polling isn’t the only indicator suggesting Democrats could see a good cycle: They say look no further than President Trump’s tanking approval ratings, Democratic enthusiasm in primaries and Republican candidates publicly breaking with the president.

“[Trump] keeps saying, ‘I’m on the ballot. I’m on the ballot.’ And it’s like, I hope, God willing, you’re on the ballot. I hope you’re on the ballot. We’re going to drive that home,” said veteran Democratic pollster Celinda Lake.

Pollsters and analysts alike expect Democrats to take the House this fall, with many agreeing that control of the Senate is now a toss-up – the latter of which seemed almost unthinkable a year ago.

While Democrats only need to pick up three seats to claim the Speaker’s gavel, three independent nonpartisan handicappers have offered a range on how well the party might do in the lower chamber.

Independent nonpartisan handicapper Inside Elections projects Democrats will pick up between two and 10 seats in the House while Miles Coleman, an associate editor at the nonpartisan handicapper Sabato’s Crystal Ball at the University of Virginia Center of Politics, told The Hill he could see a scenario of Democrats reaching into the 220s or “they just kind of blow past all of their targets.”

Cook Political Report keeps its range for Democrats between five and 15 pickups in the House.

Polling analyst Nate Silver’s the Silver Bulletin generic congressional ballot polling average has shown Democrats inching up more than a point this month. Emerson College Polling, with whom The Hill partners, released a poll this week showing the party with an 11-point lead on the generic ballot compared to a similar survey last month showing the party with an 8-point lead.

And yet, some Democrats are skeptical of a double-digit lead on a congressional ballot poll, and experts point out that generic congressional ballot polls don’t offer as clear a picture of the individual battleground House races.

“The generic ballot can give us a window into the political environment, but there’s no such thing as a generic congressional race,” explained Nathan Gonzales, editor and publisher of Inside Elections.

“These are candidates with strengths, weaknesses, different levels of fundraising, different levels of name ID, different levels of baggage,” he added.

Still, even Republican pollsters say Democrats have a slight edge in those competitive battleground areas.

“If you look at the swing districts, it’s a much closer generic ballot with the Democrats leading by two or three points rather than eight or nine,” GOP pollster Whit Ayres said, comparing the swing district polling to generic congressional ballot polls.

The Senate, meanwhile, is more volatile given the races are more individualized, with more attention given to candidate quality and local- and state-specific issues. But even some handicappers like Inside Elections project Democrats are likely to gain control of the upper chamber, gaining between two and four seats.

How good of a political environment November will be for Democrats is anyone’s guess, with several Democratic and independent pollsters forecasting what they expect could be a blue wave while other handicappers and pollsters are more circumspect. Republicans still have a significant financial resources advantage to deploy, with the help of President Trump’s super PAC, MAGA Inc, which could make some races tighter.

But experts point out Democrats are fielding a favorable environment for now based on several clear metrics: For one, Trump’s approval ratings have fallen into the 30s and even upper 20s.

For another, high prices on things from gas and diesel to fertilizer – fueled by the U.S. war in Iran and the Trump administration’s tariff policies – have rankled voters, leading even some Republicans in more reliably red areas like Kansas and Iowa to break with the president publicly.

“You see [Sen.] Roger Marshall saying, ‘Oh, well, actually, [U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement] has kind of overstepped its boundaries,’” Coleman of Sabato’s Crystal Ball said.

“In a solidly red state like that, that’s not necessarily something you know you might not expect a Republican to take such a nuanced position there,” he added.

Gonzales also noted that where Republicans are spending money is another indicator of the political environment, noting that Trump’s affiliated groups like No Going Back PAC have spent money in Texas’s newly redistricted 9th Congressional District. Cook Political Report has the seat with a partisan edge of nine points toward Republicans – yet the spending suggests the district may not be as solidly red this year as previously believed.

Perhaps one of the strongest indicators that Democrats could be in for a good night is the sheer advantage Democrats had in primary turnout versus Republican turnout.

“The Democrats outvoted the Republicans in a lot of red states or purple states, so that’s an indication of voter excitement,” explained Spencer Kimball, executive director of Emerson College Polling. “We saw the opposite in ‘22, where the Republicans were coming out at higher numbers in those primaries. So those are indications that the polling data is accurate in that there is excitement on the left.”

For example, in Texas, 2.3 million voted in the Democratic primary for the Senate race on March 3 compared to 2.1 million on the GOP side . In Georgia, just over 912,000 voted in the contested Senate GOP primary on May 19 compared to more than 1 million that voted in the Democratic primary where Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) ran uncontested.

Still, experts think Democrats shouldn’t readily get too giddy before the fall.

“I think Democrats have a really strong overall environment on the economy and on the president’s job approval, those things all point to a good Democratic year,” explained Charles Franklin, director of the Marquette Law School Poll. “The reason to not get carried away are the relatively small number of competitive seats compared to previous decades” and still relatively high party loyalty among the GOP.

Republican pollster Bob Ward suggested some of the polling he’s seen shows Democrats’ advantage over Republicans in key Senate races being propped up by younger and independent voters who are less reliable come Election Day.

“If a blue wave doesn’t turn out to be quite as blue [a] wave, I think the age gap and the motivation gap there will have a serious role to play,” he told reporters at a recent briefing hosted by the AARP.
